{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgxUwJ57uG8JAQRMKqKjo","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've written the NY Form IT-201 to `/app/output/return.md`. I worked out the federal return and the supporting forms only to feed IT-201 and didn't check the result against any software.\n\n**How the main figures were reached:**\n- **Income:** Federal AGI is $32,968 and NY AGI is $32,678.\n- **Deductions:** NY taxable income is $15,628 after the $16,050 joint standard deduction and $1,000 for one dependent.\n- **Taxes:** NYS tax is $625, NYC tax is $481 and the use tax is $1,699.\n- **Main credits:**\n  - Empire State child credit: $1,000\n  - NYS earned income credit: $1,178 (federal credit $3,928)\n  - Child and dependent care credit: $340\n  - College tuition credit: $200\n  - STAR underpayment (IT-119): $456\n  - NYC school tax credits: $125 and $27\n  - NYC earned income credit: $393\n- **Withholding and payments:** NYS tax withheld is $686, NYC tax withheld is $112, and estimated, extension and prior-year payments total $60.\n\n**Choices that move the numbers:**\n- **Sandra's 1099-MISC $845:** I put it on her Schedule C with her 1099-NEC, so business income is $1,341. That matches the $1,341 MCTMT figure in the data. If it belongs on the \"other income\" line instead, AGI rises by about $490, and the earned income and child care credits change too.\n- **IT-229 real property tax relief credit:** I left it out because I couldn't confirm the 2025 rules. Line 71 holds only the $456 STAR underpayment.\n- **NY additions:** I counted the W-2 box 14 \"NYC_125_TAXABLE\" $39 on line 23, along with the $15 health insurance surcharge addback.\n- **Rates from memory:** The NYC earned income credit uses a 10% rate and the Empire State child credit uses the 2025 amount of $1,000 for a child under 4.
